title: Wrong IP Address
topology: Basic LAN
symptom: PC1 cannot ping PC2
topology_note: PC1 and PC2 are connected to the same switch. PC2 uses 192.168.1.20/24. PC1 is intentionally configured with an IP from a different network.
show_outputs: PC1 ipconfig: IP Address: 192.168.2.10 Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0 Default Gateway: 0.0.0.0
expected_fault: PC1 has an incorrect IP address and is in a different network from PC2.

title: Wrong Subnet Mask
topology: Two LANs connected by Router
symptom: PC1 cannot ping PC2
topology_note: PC1 is in the 192.168.1.0/24 network and PC2 is in the 192.168.2.0/24 network. The router connects both networks. PC1 is intentionally configured with an incorrect subnet mask.
show_outputs: PC1 ipconfig: IP Address: 192.168.1.10 Subnet Mask: 255.255.0.0 Default Gateway: 192.168.1.1
expected_fault: PC1 has an incorrect subnet mask. The correct subnet mask is 255.255.255.0.

title: Wrong Default Gateway
topology: Two LANs connected by Router
symptom: PC1 cannot reach PC2
topology_note: PC1 is connected to the 192.168.1.0/24 network. PC2 is connected to the 192.168.2.0/24 network. Router G0/0 is 192.168.1.1 and G0/1 is 192.168.2.1. PC1 is intentionally configured with the wrong default gateway.
show_outputs: PC1 ipconfig: IP Address: 192.168.1.10 Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0 Default Gateway: 192.168.2.1
expected_fault: PC1 ipconfig: IP Address: 192.168.1.10 Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0 Default Gateway: 192.168.2.1

title: Interface ShutdownTwo LANs connected by Router
symptom: PC1 cannot reach PC2
topology_note: PC1 is connected to the 192.168.1.0/24 network and PC2 is connected to the 192.168.2.0/24 network. Router G0/0 connects to PC1's network and G0/1 connects to PC2's network. G0/1 is intentionally shut down.
show_outputs: Router show ip interface brief: GigabitEthernet0/0 192.168.1.1 up GigabitEthernet0/1 192.168.2.1 administratively down
expected_fault: GigabitEthernet0/1 is administratively down.

title: Missing VLAN
topology: Two PCs connected to one switch
symptom: PC1 cannot communicate as expected with its assigned network.
topology_note: PC1 is connected to FastEthernet0/1 and should belong to VLAN 10. PC2 is connected to FastEthernet0/2 and belongs to VLAN 20. VLAN 10 was intentionally removed from the switch configuration.
show_outputs: VLAN 10 is missing. show running-config interface fastEthernet 0/1: The interface is configured for access VLAN 10.
expected_fault: VLAN 10 is missing from the switch configuration.

title: Wrong Access VLAN
topology: Two PCs connected to one switch
symptom: PC1 is unable to communicate with devices in its expected VLAN.
topology_note: PC1 is connected to FastEthernet0/1 and should belong to VLAN 10. PC2 is connected to FastEthernet0/2 and belongs to VLAN 20. Both VLANs exist, but PC1's switch port is intentionally assigned to VLAN 20.
show_outputs: VLAN 10 = STAFF VLAN 20 = STUDENTS Fa0/1 appears under VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10. show running-config interface fastEthernet 0/1: switchport mode access switchport access vlan 20
expected_fault: FastEthernet0/1 is assigned to the wrong access VLAN. It should be assigned to VLAN 10.

title: Trunk Configuration Problem
topology: Two switches connected with PCs in VLAN 10
symptom: PC1 cannot communicate with PC2 even though both PCs are configured in VLAN 10.
topology_note: PC1 is connected to Switch1 and PC2 is connected to Switch2. Both PCs belong to VLAN 10. Switch1 and Switch2 are connected through FastEthernet0/24. The link is intentionally configured as an access port instead of a trunk.
show_outputs: Switch1 show interfaces trunk: Fa0/24 is not listed as an active trunk. Switch1 show interfaces fastEthernet 0/24 switchport: Administrative Mode: static access
expected_fault: The Switch1-to-Switch2 link is not configured as a trunk. It should use switchport mode trunk.

title: VLAN Allowed List Mismatch
topology: Two switches connected by a trunk with PCs in VLAN 10
symptom: PC1 cannot communicate with PC2 even though both PCs belong to VLAN 10 and the switch-to-switch link is a trunk.
topology_note: PC1 is connected to Switch1 and PC2 is connected to Switch2. Both PCs belong to VLAN 10. The switch-to-switch link uses FastEthernet0/24 as a trunk. Switch1 allows VLAN 10 on the trunk, while Switch2 is intentionally configured to allow VLAN 20 instead.
show_outputs: Switch1 show interfaces trunk: VLAN 10 is allowed on Fa0/24. Switch2 show interfaces trunk: VLAN 20 is allowed on Fa0/24 and VLAN 10 is not allowed.
expected_fault: The allowed VLAN configuration is mismatched between the two trunk interfaces. VLAN 10 must be allowed on both sides.

title: Missing Inter-VLAN Subinterface
topology: Two VLANs connected to one switch and one router
symptom: PC1 in VLAN 10 cannot communicate with PC2 in VLAN 20.
topology_note: PC1 belongs to VLAN 10 with IP 192.168.10.10. PC2 belongs to VLAN 20 with IP 192.168.20.10. The switch-to-router link is a trunk. Router subinterface G0/0.10 exists, but G0/0.20 is intentionally removed.
show_outputs: show ip interface brief: GigabitEthernet0/0.10 = 192.168.10.1 GigabitEthernet0/0.20 is missing. show running-config: G0/0.10 configuration exists. G0/0.20 configuration is absent.
expected_fault: The router is missing the G0/0.20 subinterface required for VLAN 20.

title: Wrong VLAN Encapsulation
topology: Two VLANs connected to one switch and one router using router-on-a-stick
symptom: PC1 in VLAN 10 cannot communicate with PC2 in VLAN 20.
topology_note: PC1 belongs to VLAN 10 and PC2 belongs to VLAN 20. The switch-to-router link is a trunk. Router subinterface G0/0.20 should handle VLAN 20, but its 802.1Q encapsulation is intentionally configured for VLAN 30.
show_outputs: show running-config: interface GigabitEthernet0/0.20 encapsulation dot1Q 30 ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0 expected_fault: G0/0.20 has the wrong 802.1Q VLAN ID. It should use encapsulation dot1Q 20.

title: Missing Subinterface
topology: Two VLANs connected to one switch and one router using router-on-a-stick
symptom: PC1 in VLAN 10 cannot communicate with PC2 in VLAN 20.
topology_note: PC1 belongs to VLAN 10 with IP 192.168.10.10. PC2 belongs to VLAN 20 with IP 192.168.20.10. The switch-to-router link is a trunk. The router's G0/0.20 subinterface is intentionally removed.
show_outputs: show ip interface brief: G0/0.10 = 192.168.10.1 up/up G0/0.20 is missing. show running-config: G0/0.10 configuration exists. G0/0.20 configuration is absent.
expected_fault: The router is missing the G0/0.20 subinterface required for VLAN 20.

title: DHCP Pool Missing
topology: One PC connected to a switch and router
topology_note: PC1 is connected to the router through a switch. The router interface is 192.168.10.1/24. The DHCP pool for the 192.168.10.0/24 network is intentionally removed.
show_outputs: PC1 ipconfig: PC1 does not receive a 192.168.10.x DHCP address and may receive a 169.254.x.x address. Router show running-config | section dhcp: No DHCP pool for LAN1 exists. Router show ip dhcp pool: Expected DHCP pool is missing.
expected_fault: The DHCP pool for the 192.168.10.0/24 network is missing.

title: Wrong DHCP Network
topology: One PC connected to a switch and router
symptom: PC1 cannot obtain a valid IP address from DHCP.
topology_note: The router interface is 192.168.10.1/24, so the actual LAN is 192.168.10.0/24. The DHCP pool is intentionally configured for 192.168.20.0/24 instead.
show_outputs: PC1 ipconfig: 169.254.x.x or DHCP request failure. Router show ip interface brief: GigabitEthernet0/0 192.168.10.1 up up Router show running-config | section dhcp: ip dhcp pool LAN1 network 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0 default-router 192.168.20.1
expected_fault: The DHCP pool is configured for the wrong network. It should use 192.168.10.0/24.

title: Wrong DHCP Gateway
topology: One PC connected to a switch and router
symptom: PC receives an IP address through DHCP but cannot correctly reach networks outside its local subnet.
topology_note: PC1 is connected to the 192.168.10.0/24 network. The router interface is 192.168.10.1. The DHCP pool is correctly configured for the 192.168.10.0/24 network, but it intentionally provides 192.168.10.254 as the default gateway.
show_outputs: PC1 ipconfig: IP Address: 192.168.10.x Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0 Default Gateway: 192.168.10.254 Router show ip interface brief: GigabitEthernet0/0 192.168.10.1 up up Router show running-config | section dhcp: ip dhcp pool LAN1 network 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0 default-router 192.168.10.254 dns-server 8.8.8.8
expected_fault: The DHCP pool provides the wrong default gateway. It should provide 192.168.10.1.

title: DHCP Addresses Exhausted
topology: Multiple PCs connected to a switch and router
symptom: A new PC cannot obtain an IP address through DHCP even though the DHCP pool and network configuration are correct.
topology_note: The router provides DHCP for the 192.168.10.0/24 network. Almost all addresses are intentionally excluded from the DHCP pool, leaving only one usable address. The first PC receives the available address, leaving no free addresses for additional clients.
show_outputs: PC1 ipconfig: IP Address: 192.168.10.254 Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0 Default Gateway: 192.168.10.1 PC2: DHCP request failed or receives a 169.254.x.x address. Router show ip dhcp binding: 192.168.10.254 is already leased. Router show ip dhcp pool: DHCP pool exists but has no available addresses.
expected_fault: The DHCP address pool is exhausted because all available addresses have been leased or excluded.

title: Missing Route
topology: Two LANs connected through two routers
symptom: PC1 cannot communicate with a PC on a different network.
topology_note: PC1 is on 192.168.10.0/24 behind Router1. PC2 is on 192.168.20.0/24 behind Router2. The routers are connected through a transit network. The route to the remote LAN is intentionally missing.
show_outputs: Router1 show ip route: No route for 192.168.20.0/24. PC1 ping 192.168.20.10: Request timed out.
expected_fault: Router1 is missing a route to the 192.168.20.0/24 destination network.

title: Wrong Static Route
topology: Two LANs connected through two routers
symptom: PC1 cannot reach the remote network even though a static route exists.
topology_note: PC1 is on 192.168.10.0/24 and the remote LAN is 192.168.20.0/24. A static route is configured on Router1, but the destination network or next-hop address is intentionally incorrect.
show_outputs: Router1 show ip route: Static route exists but points to an incorrect destination or next hop. PC1 ping 192.168.20.10: Request timed out.
expected_fault: The static route contains an incorrect destination network, subnet mask, or next-hop address.

title: Router Interface Down
topology: LAN connected to a router
symptom: Devices connected to one router interface cannot communicate with the network.
topology_note: The router provides the gateway for the LAN. The interface connected to the LAN is intentionally shut down.
show_outputs: show ip interface brief: The affected interface shows administratively down/down. PC ping to gateway: Request timed out.
expected_fault: The router interface connected to the LAN is administratively down.

title: Wrong Network Address
topology: LAN connected to a router
symptom: The router configuration does not match the actual LAN network.
topology_note: The LAN uses one network range, but the router or routing configuration is intentionally configured with a different network address.
show_outputs: show ip interface brief: Router interface uses an IP from the wrong network. show ip route: Connected network does not match the expected LAN network.
expected_fault: The configured network address does not match the actual LAN network.

title: Wrong DNS Server
topology: PC connected to LAN and DNS server
symptom: The PC can communicate using IP addresses but cannot resolve domain names.
topology_note: The PC has a valid IP address and gateway, but its DNS configuration points to an incorrect DNS server address.
show_outputs: PC ipconfig: Valid IP and gateway but incorrect DNS server. Ping server IP: Successful. Ping hostname: Fails to resolve.
expected_fault: The PC or DHCP configuration specifies the wrong DNS server address.

title: Missing DNS Record
topology: PC connected to DNS server and internal server
symptom: The DNS server is reachable, but the internal server hostname cannot be resolved.
topology_note: The PC can reach the DNS server and the internal server by IP address. The required hostname-to-IP record is intentionally missing from the DNS service.
show_outputs: PC ping DNS server IP: Successful. PC ping internal server IP: Successful. PC ping internal-server hostname: Name resolution fails.
expected_fault: The required DNS A record for the internal server hostname is missing.

title: DNS Server Unreachable
topology: PC connected to LAN and DNS server
symptom: The PC has network connectivity but cannot reach the configured DNS server.
topology_note: The PC is configured with a DNS server address, but routing or connectivity to that DNS server is intentionally broken.
show_outputs: PC ipconfig: Correct IP, subnet mask, gateway and DNS server. Ping DNS server: Request timed out. Hostname resolution: Fails.
expected_fault: The configured DNS server is unreachable because of a network connectivity or routing problem.

title: ACL Blocks Traffic
topology: PC connected through router with an ACL
symptom: Traffic that should be allowed is blocked by an access control list.
topology_note: The router has an ACL applied to the traffic path. The ACL intentionally contains a deny statement that blocks the required source or destination traffic.
show_outputs: show access-lists: ACL contains a deny rule matching the required traffic. PC ping/server access: Fails.
expected_fault: An ACL deny rule is blocking traffic that should be permitted.

title: ACL on Wrong Interface
topology: PC connected through router with an ACL
symptom: The ACL does not control the intended traffic because it is applied to the wrong interface.
topology_note: The ACL rules themselves are correct, but the ACL is intentionally applied inbound or outbound on an interface that does not carry the intended traffic.
show_outputs: show access-lists: ACL rules are correct. show running-config: ACL is applied to the wrong router interface or direction.
expected_fault: The ACL is applied to the wrong interface or direction.

title: Wrong ACL Order
topology: PC connected through router with an ACL
symptom: Allowed traffic is blocked even though a permit rule exists in the ACL.
topology_note: The ACL contains both deny and permit statements, but the deny statement is intentionally placed before the permit statement for the same traffic.
show_outputs: show access-lists: Deny rule appears before the required permit rule. PC traffic: Blocked.
expected_fault: The ACL rule order is incorrect. A deny rule is matched before the intended permit rule.

title: NAT Missing
topology: Private LAN connected to an external network through a router
symptom: Private LAN hosts cannot access the external network because their private addresses are not translated.
topology_note: The router connects a private LAN to an external network. NAT is intentionally not configured on the router.
show_outputs: show running-config: No NAT configuration. show ip nat translations: No translations. Private PC access to external server: Fails.
expected_fault: NAT configuration is missing from the router.

title: NAT Inside/Outside Mistake
topology: Private LAN connected to an external network through a router
symptom: NAT is configured but translation does not work correctly.
topology_note: The router has NAT configured, but the LAN and external interfaces are intentionally assigned incorrect ip nat inside or ip nat outside roles.
show_outputs: show running-config: NAT inside/outside roles are reversed or assigned to the wrong interfaces. show ip nat translations: No expected translations. Private PC access: Fails.
expected_fault: The router interfaces have incorrect NAT inside/outside configuration.

title: NAT ACL Mismatch
topology: Private LAN connected to an external network through a router
symptom: Private hosts cannot access the external network even though NAT is configured.
topology_note: The NAT configuration and inside/outside interfaces exist, but the ACL used by NAT does not match the actual private LAN subnet.
show_outputs: show access-lists: NAT ACL matches the wrong network. show ip nat translations: No translation for the actual private client. Private PC access: Fails.
expected_fault: The NAT ACL does not permit the actual private LAN addresses.

title: Wireless Configuration Problem
topology: Wireless PC connected to a wireless router or access point
symptom: The wireless client cannot connect to the configured Wi-Fi network.
topology_note: The wireless router or access point is configured with an incorrect SSID, security mode, or wireless password.
show_outputs: Wireless device configuration: SSID or security settings do not match the client. Wireless PC: Cannot associate with the wireless network.
expected_fault: Wireless configuration is incorrect, such as a wrong SSID, security mode, or password.

title: Wireless ? Internal Server Problem
topology: Wireless client connected to an internal wired server through a router
symptom: The wireless client connects to Wi-Fi successfully but cannot reach the internal server.
topology_note: The wireless client receives a valid IP address and can communicate with the wireless network, but routing, gateway, VLAN, or access configuration prevents access to the internal server.
show_outputs: Wireless PC ipconfig: Valid wireless IP and gateway. Ping wireless gateway: Successful. Ping internal server: Fails. Router routing/ACL configuration: Contains the connectivity fault.
expected_fault: The wireless client can reach its local network but cannot reach the internal server because of an internal routing, gateway, VLAN, or access configuration problem.
